title: People Want to Be Part of Something Special
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article explores how leaders manufacture the feeling of 'special' for their teams, even when an organization lacks a grand, world-changing vision. It identifies several levers available to leaders: assembling and nurturing genuinely talented teams, designing unique shared experiences, and building deep, individualized relationships with team members. The piece notes that even organizations with underperforming or toxic cultures can still create pockets of specialness under the right leader, and closes by challenging readers to consider whether they are actively in the business of creating that feeling for their people.
points: Feeling part of something special drives pride, confidence, and sustained effort.
Not every organization has a grand vision, but leaders can still manufacture special experiences.
Assembling talented teams and designing unique shared experiences are two levers leaders can pull.
Building deep, individualized relationships with team members also creates a feeling of specialness.
Even leaders in underperforming or toxic cultures can create pockets of specialness for their people.
quotes: Special promotes pride, confidence, and passion. When part of something special, team members are highly motivated to sustain that specialness through their hard work, innovation, and commitment.
Unfortunately, special doesn’t fall from the sky. It takes leaders to create something special for the benefit of everyone involved.
Good leaders don’t need to rely on visions and long-term goals to create special.
Even in organizations that are underperforming or with toxic cultures, the best leaders can create a heaven inside a hell.
Everyone wants to be a part of something special and to feel special in how they are treated.
As a leader, are you in the business of creating special? Read the fine print. It’s in the job description.
